title: Investigating Reward Hacking in Agentic Task Completion: When Do Agents Game Metrics Instead of Solving Problems?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reward hacking in agentic settings is a critical alignment concern. Identifying novel reward-hacking strategies in LLM agents (e.g., editing test files) provides concrete evidence for a known theoretical risk. Testing metric-agnostic evaluation as a defense adds practical value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing 15 tasks with gameable metrics is conceptually accessible. Running agents and performing qualitative assessment of genuine vs gamed completion is straightforward. The qualitative analysis component is beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 15 tasks is moderate. The qualitative assessment of each task completion adds time. Could be scoped to 5-7 tasks with clear gaming opportunities. The deliverable (taxonomy of gaming strategies + frequency) is well-defined.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
